title: Use electronic mail to send and receive messages

lessons.title: Email basics
lessons.html:
What email is

Electronic mail (email) is a way to send written messages and files from one computer or phone to another over the internet. In a farm workshop or equipment dealership you can use email to order parts, send quotes, receive service bulletins from manufacturers and report to your manager.

Email addresses

An email address looks like this: name@company.co.za. It has a user name, the @ sign (said 'at') and the domain, which is usually the company or email provider. An address must be typed exactly right or the message will not arrive.

Email programs

You may use a program like Outlook or Thunderbird, or a webmail service in the browser, or an app on your phone. They all have similar parts:

  • Inbox: messages you have received.
  • Sent: messages you have sent.
  • Drafts: messages you started but did not send.
  • Trash or Deleted items: messages you deleted.
  • Junk or Spam: messages the system thinks are unwanted.
  • Contacts or Address book: saved email addresses.

Logging in safely

  1. Open the email program or web page.
  2. Type your user name and password.
  3. Never share your password with anyone, not even co-workers.
  4. Log out when you finish on a shared computer.

Reading messages

In the inbox, unread messages are usually shown in bold. Click a message to open it. You can see who sent it (From), when, the subject and the message. If there is a paperclip symbol, there is an attachment, such as a parts list or a photo.

lessons.title: Writing and sending messages
lessons.html:
Creating a new email

  1. Click New or Compose.
  2. In To, type the address of the main person.
  3. In Cc (carbon copy), add people who must see the message but do not need to act, such as your supervisor.
  4. Bcc (blind carbon copy) hides addresses from other receivers. Use it when sending to many outside people.
  5. Type a short, clear Subject, for example 'Order: 2 fuel filters for tractor T05'.
  6. Type your message in the body.
  7. Check it and click Send.

Writing a good work email

  • Start with a greeting: 'Good morning Mr Dlamini'.
  • Say what you want in the first line.
  • Give details: part numbers, quantities, machine model and serial number, date needed.
  • Keep it short and polite.
  • End with 'Thank you' or 'Regards', your name, job and phone number.
  • Do not type in all capital letters. It looks like shouting.

Example

Subject: Quote request – hydraulic hose for baler

Good morning Sipho. Please send me a quote for one hydraulic hose, part number as in the attached photo, for our baler. We need it by Friday. Thank you. Lerato, Workshop Assistant, 082 000 0000.

Attachments

To send a file, click the paperclip or Attach, find the file and click Open. Wait for it to upload before sending. Large files may not go through. Mention the attachment in your message.

Reply and forward

  • Reply answers only the sender.
  • Reply All answers everyone on the message. Use it carefully.
  • Forward sends the message to someone new.

lessons.title: Managing email and staying safe
lessons.html:
Keeping your inbox in order

  • Read and reply to work emails quickly.
  • Create folders, such as 'Parts orders' or 'Service bulletins', and move messages into them.
  • Delete messages you do not need.
  • Use the search box to find old messages by name or word.
  • Save important attachments in the correct folder on the computer.
  • Add regular suppliers to your contacts.

Email safety

Criminals use email to steal money and information. This is called phishing.

  • Do not open attachments or click links from people you do not know.
  • Be careful of messages that say 'urgent', ask for your password, or say you won a prize.
  • Check the sender's address. A fake one may look almost like the real one.
  • If a supplier emails to say their bank details have changed, do not pay. Phone the supplier on a number you already know to check. Tell your manager.
  • Never send your password or ID number by email.
  • Report suspicious emails to your manager or IT person.

Good email manners

  • Be polite and respectful. Emails can be forwarded and kept for a long time.
  • Do not send jokes, chain letters or offensive pictures from a work account.
  • Do not share private company or worker information with people outside.
  • Think before you click Reply All.

When email is not the best way

For an emergency, such as a fire or an injury, phone or call for help in person. Email is too slow for emergencies.

Key points

  • An email address has a user name, the @ sign and a domain.
  • Use a clear subject and put the main request in the first line.
  • Cc copies people in; Bcc hides addresses.
  • Check attachments before sending and mention them in the message.
  • Never open unknown attachments or give your password; check bank detail changes by phone.
